{{Short description|Defined statistical regions of the United States}}
{{U.S. city population tables}}
The [[Federal government of the United States|United States federal government]] defines and delineates the nation's [[metropolitan area]]s for statistical purposes, using a set of standard '''statistical area''' definitions. {{As of|2023|post=,}} the U.S. [[Office of Management and Budget]] (OMB) defined and delineated 393 [[metropolitan statistical area]]s (MSAs) and 542 [[micropolitan statistical area]]s (μSAs) in the United States and Puerto Rico.<ref name="OMB_23-01">{{cite web|url=https://bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/OMB-Bulletin-23-01.pdf|title=OMB Bulletin No. 23-01: Revised Delineations of Metropolitan Statistical Areas, Micropolitan Statistical Areas, and Combined Statistical Areas, and Guidance on Uses of the Delineations of These Areas|date=July 21, 2023|publisher=[[United States Office of Management and Budget]]|access-date=May 2, 2024}}</ref> Many of these 935 MSAs and μSAs are, in turn, components of larger [[combined statistical area]]s (CSAs) consisting of adjacent MSAs and μSAs that are linked by [[commuting]] ties; {{as of|2023|lc=y|post=,}} 582 metropolitan and micropolitan areas are components of the 184 defined CSAs. 

Metropolitan and micropolitan statistical areas are defined as consisting of one or more adjacent [[county (United States)|counties]] or [[county-equivalent|county equivalents]] with at least one [[List of United States urban areas|urban core area]] meeting relevant population thresholds, plus adjacent territory that has a high degree of social and [[economic integration]] with the core, as measured by commuting ties. A metropolitan statistical area has at least one [[urban area|core]] with a population of at least 50,000. In a micropolitan statistical area, the largest core has a population of at least 10,000 but less than 50,000.

==Maps==
[[File:CBSA WallMap Jul2023.pdf|left|thumb|720x720px|An enlargeable map of the 935 [[core-based statistical area]]s (MSAs and μSAs) of the [[U.S. state|50 states]], the [[Washington, D.C.|District of Columbia]], and [[Puerto Rico]]. The 393 MSAs are shown in medium green {{color box|#008060}}. The 542 μSAs are shown in light green {{color box|#609f8f}}.]]
[[File:CSA WallMap Jul2023.pdf|left|thumb|720x720px|An enlargeable map of the 184 combined statistical areas (CSAs) of the [[U.S. state|50 states]], the [[Washington, D.C.|District of Columbia]], and [[Puerto Rico]], shown in <span style="color:#008060;">shades of green</span>. The [[metropolitan statistical area]]s (MSAs) outside CSAs are shown in <span style="color:#FF9300;">medium tan</span>.  The [[micropolitan statistical area]]s (μSAs) outside CSAs are shown in <span style="color:#FFC980;">light tan</span>.]]
{{clear}}
